lessons.title: Grid View: Rows, Columns and the fr Unit

objectives.cognitive: Explain what display: grid does to a box's children, and what grid-template-columns, fr, gap and auto-fit control.
objectives.affective: Value a layout that answers the width of the page instead of one fixed screen.
objectives.psychomotor: Turn Juan's gallery and project cards into grids in CodeShare.

blocks.markdown: **How to use this module:** Work in order, Monday to Friday. Run every sample unchanged first, then do its small task. Answer each day's exit slip after its last step.

**Everything happens in CodeShare.** Open your class, then **Module**, this week and a step. **Work in code editor** loads the step's sample files into the editor tabs; **Run code** shows the step's run page in the page window and checks it, and its links open the project's other pages there. It works online and from the classroom laptop; no internet, installation, download or account is needed.

**Reading the outputs:** an output box shows the page text CodeShare checks for the step's run page: the Tab title, the Visible page text, then, on Steps 1, 3, 4, 7, 8 and 9, Media checks. Grids, gaps and pictures that resize move boxes only, so most steps this week leave the output exactly as it was; Step 8, the broken one, is the only sample that changes it. Spaces count.

**Where we start:** Juan's finished Week 9 site (three pages and styles.css) carries forward in your module project. This is the last week: by Friday the same site answers every width. Each step loads its run page and every file it needs; boxes show only new or changed lines.
**Week 10 starts here:** Juan's gallery and project cards are flex rows that wrap: they fill a line and break where they run out, instead of standing in real columns.

display: grid makes a box a grid container, and every child becomes a grid item laid out in rows and columns. grid-template-columns names the columns: repeat(2, 1fr) is two, and fr gives each a fraction of the space that is left. gap sets the space between the cells in one place. repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr)) lets the grid count its own columns. A grid item is a box of its own, so the output still gives it its own line.
A tray of pandesal: the tray is the container and the rolls are the items. The baker does not place each roll by hand; the tray's rows and columns do it, and a wider tray takes another column.

the gallery, the two tables, the cards

blocks.markdown: **Media steps:** Steps 1, 3, 4, 7, 8 and 9 run index.html, with Juan's picture, sound, video, gallery pictures and, from Step 3, his new banner — files your teacher adds under Media files. Online, CodeShare checks them automatically; Run code waits on Loading media… until they are on this device. Offline, these six steps show Checked by your teacher for now, and your teacher presses Mark done. Steps 2, 5 and 6 run projects.html and are checked automatically.

blocks.instruction: Juan's Week 9 site carries forward. A grid view lays boxes out in rows and columns at once. display: grid makes a box a grid container and its children grid items; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr) asks for two columns, and the fr unit shares out the space that is left, so each takes one half. gap: 12px spaces the cells. Juan's gallery was a flex row that wrapped; now it is a grid of two equal columns, and each figure fills the column it is given. Run index.html unchanged.

blocks.markdown: **Practice: does it change the output?** (a) display: grid on .gallery; (b) gap: 40px instead of 12px; (c) repeat(4, 1fr) instead of repeat(2, 1fr); (d) a template class with text-transform: uppercase. Answers: (a) no: a figure was already a box of its own; (b) no: spacing is not page text; (c) no: each figure keeps its own line; (d) yes: the letters themselves change.

**Page checks and the width of the window:** a page check reads a computed value, so it must be a value that is the same at every width. A column's real width is not: a track in fr, minmax() or auto-fit is worked out from the space there is, so it is never the same number twice. That is why the checks read display, the gap, max-width and the counts, never a column width, and why you test the width yourself by making the browser window narrower.
Answer the Monday exit slip now.

In Week 9 the gallery was a flex row with flex-wrap: wrap. What does repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr)) in Step 2 do instead?

lessons.title: Pictures and Video That Fit Any Width

objectives.cognitive: Explain why max-width: 100% with height: auto keeps a picture or video inside the page.
objectives.affective: Show care for classmates whose only computer is a phone with a small screen.
objectives.psychomotor: Make Juan's banner, gallery pictures, profile picture and video resize in CodeShare.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** Juan's pictures and video have fixed widths, so a picture wider than the page would push the whole page sideways.

max-width: 100% means never wider than the box around it, and max-width overrides any width. height: auto lets the height follow the width, so the shape is kept. The width and height in the HTML stay the natural size. For one picture in several real sizes there are srcset and sizes, which name a file and its width in w units; this module uses one file per picture.

A tarpaulin for the barangay fiesta: the same design is printed smaller for a narrow wall, keeping its shape. One cut for a wide wall and nailed to a narrow one hangs over the edge: that is a picture with no max-width.

the height follows the width, so the shape is kept
without it a picture is squashed
the natural size, and the room the browser keeps for it
keep both; they are not CSS

blocks.instruction: A picture wider than the page pushes the whole page sideways. Juan's new banner is 900 pixels wide, so .banner gets max-width: 100%: never wider than the box it sits in. max-width overrides width, and the percentage is measured against that box; height: auto keeps the shape. The gallery pictures get the same two lines instead of a fixed width. Run index.html unchanged.

lessons.title: Every Width Checked, Then the Hardest Repair

objectives.cognitive: Recognise an invalid value, a missing bracket, a query with no unit and a picture that overflows.
objectives.affective: Show patience when one missing bracket undoes the rest of a stylesheet.
objectives.psychomotor: Lay the two tables out in a grid, repair the broken gallery rule, and finish the personal resume.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** Juan's two tables each take a whole page width, and a missing bracket would be invisible to him.

An invalid value such as display: gird drops only its own declaration. A grid property written on the items instead of the container does nothing. A missing bracket is worse: the value is never finished, so everything after it is swallowed. @media (max-width: 900), with no unit, is dropped whole. A picture with a fixed width wider than the page makes the page scroll sideways.
An announcement on the barangay bulletin board that stops in the middle of a sentence: everything written after it is lost too, because nobody can tell where the first notice ended.

blocks.instruction: Now the whole site is checked at every width. Juan's two education tables each took a whole page width. They go into one div with class="tables", a section around each heading and its table, and .tables is a grid of repeat(auto-fit, minmax(340px, 1fr)): two columns when they fit, one when they do not, and a query makes that certain at 900px and narrower. Run index.html unchanged.

performanceTask.title: My Resume, Week 10: My Complete Responsive Resume
performanceTask.markdown:
The last performance task of the course. Start Thursday, finish and present Friday. In CodeShare open Projects, then Personal performance-task project: your Week 9 site carries forward, and this week you finish it.

Make your resume answer the width of the page. Lay at least one part of it out as a grid: display: grid on the container, your own grid-template-columns (repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr)) is a good start) and gap. Give every picture and your video max-width: 100% and height: auto. Add at least one media query of your own, @media (max-width: 900px), that improves the narrow layout; nothing inside it may add, remove or re-letter a word. Keep your colours from the chart on page 13 (4.5:1 for text).

Your own project's page fills the page window, so it is wider than a module step's: widen the browser window, then make it narrower, and watch your query turn on. The page window follows the browser window and cannot be dragged on its own.

Use only safe details: no home address, phone number, birth date, ID numbers or social media, and no other people in a picture. Run code until index.html runs with no error, then press Submit this version.

Thursday: 0–60 min, Steps 7–8 and the strip; 60–120 min, plan, show the teacher, start. Friday: 0–30 min, finish and run; 30–105 min, presentations; 105–120 min, strip and Submit this version.
checklist: Keep your Week 9 site: every page, the nav, the gallery, your states and flex containers, styles.css everywhere.
At least one grid of your own: display: grid with your own grid-template-columns and gap.
max-width: 100% and height: auto on every picture and the video, with their width and height still in the HTML.
At least one media query of your own, @media (max-width: 900px), with its unit.
Nothing inside a query adds, removes or re-letters a word: the output is the same at every width.
Readable colours from the chart; nothing in url(); no address, phone, birth date, ID numbers, social media or other people.
Run code with no error at a wide and a narrow browser window; Submit this version, then present.
